items.sourceEnglish: Plant Selection & Guilds
items.draft: Khetho ya Mimela na Guilds
items.blindBackTranslation: Selection of Plants and Guilds

items.sourceEnglish: Choose useful plant partners, return mulch and manage the guild as trees grow.
items.draft: Khethani mimela ya ndeme ine ya shumisana, vhuyedzani mulch, ni ṱhogomele guild musi miri i tshi gula.
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose important plants that work together, return mulch, and take care of the guild when the trees are growing.

items.sourceEnglish: These bacteria convert nitrogen from the air into forms the legume can use.
items.draft: Heyi zwipuka zwiṱuku (bacteria) zwi shandukisa nitrogen i bvaho moyani u vha zwivhumbeo zwine legume ya nga zwi shumisa.
items.blindBackTranslation: These small plants change nitrogen that comes from the air into forms that a legume can use.

items.sourceEnglish: Find nodules on a spare legume plant. Nodulation and growth depend on the plant, suitable bacteria and growing conditions.
items.draft: Wanani nodules kha mumela wa legume une wa si ṱoḓee. Nodulation na u gula zwi ḓitika nga mumela, zwipuka zwiṱuku zwo teaho (bacteria) na zwiimiswa zwa u gula.
items.blindBackTranslation: Find nodules on the legume plant that you do not want [?]. Nodulation and growth depend on the plant, suitable small animals/insects [?] and growth conditions.

items.sourceEnglish: Return suitable leafy prunings, fallen leaves and crop residues as mulch. Soil organisms release nutrients during decomposition.
items.draft: Vhuyedzani malavhi a matari o gwiwaho a teaho, matari o welaho na zwisalela zwa zwijalo sa mulch. Zwipuka zwa mavuni zwi ṋea nutrients musi decomposition i tshi itea.
items.blindBackTranslation: Return suitable cut branches, fallen leaves and plant remains as mulch. The leaves of plants give nutrients when decomposition takes place.

items.sourceEnglish: This takes time. A living legume is not an instant fertiliser pipe into the fruit tree.
items.draft: Izwi zwi dzhia tshifhinga. Legume i tshilaho a si phaiphi i ṱavhanyaho ya u isa fertiliser kha muri wa mitshelo.
items.blindBackTranslation: This takes time. A living legume is not a fast pipe for taking fertiliser to the fruit tree.

items.sourceEnglish: It is indigenous to KwaZulu-Natal. In suitable warm conditions, manage this short-lived shrub or small tree as a support plant.
items.draft: I indigenous kha KwaZulu-Natal. Kha zwiimiswa zwo teaho zwa u fhisa ha ḓuvha, ṱhogomelani heyi tshiri kana muri muṱuku une wa tshila tshifhinga tshipfufhi sa support plant.
items.blindBackTranslation: It is indigenous in KwaZulu-Natal. In suitable conditions of daytime heat, look after this shrub or small tree that lives for a short time as a support plant.

items.sourceEnglish: Allow room for its growth. Prune for mulch and reassess it when shade or water competition increases.
items.draft: Ṋeani vhupo ha u gula ha yo. Gwani malavhi u itela mulch ni i sedzese hafhu musi ṱhundu kana u lwisana nga madi zwi tshi engedzea.
items.blindBackTranslation: Give it its growing space. Cut the branches for mulch and check it again when pests [?] or competition for water increase.

items.sourceEnglish: Sesbania punicea is the invasive red sesbania. Its pods have four lengthwise wings. Confirm identity using reliable botanical guidance.
items.draft: Sesbania punicea ndi red sesbania i re invasive. Zwikhwama zwayo zwa mbeu (pods) zwi na mapapi mana a tshi ya nga vhulapfu ha zwikhwama. Khwaṱhisedzani uri ndi mini ni tshi shumisa botanical guidance i fulufhedzeaho.
items.blindBackTranslation: Sesbania punicea is red sesbania, which is invasive. Its seed pods have four wings [?] running along the length of the pods. Confirm what you use as reliable botanical guidance.

items.sourceEnglish: Check the full name before planting. Respect the agreed project species list, including any restriction on Sesbania sesban.
items.draft: Sedzani dzina ḽo fhelelaho phanḓa ha u sima. Ṱhonifhani project species list yo tendelanwaho, hu tshi katelwa thivhelo ifhio na ifhio kha Sesbania sesban.
items.blindBackTranslation: Check the full name before planting. Respect the approved project species list, including whatever restriction there is on Sesbania sesban.

items.sourceEnglish: Use a sunny, freely draining position. It is a short-lived support shrub; frost and waterlogging can limit it.
items.draft: Shumisani vhupo ha ḓuvha hune mavu a kovhela madi zwavhuḓi. Ndi support shrub i tshilaho tshifhinga tshipfufhi; mutsho wa frost na u dzula ha madi mavuni zwi nga i thivhela.
items.blindBackTranslation: Use a sunny place where the soil drains water well. It is a short-lived support shrub; frost cold and water standing in the soil can hinder it.

items.sourceEnglish: Decide whether each plant mainly supplies peas or leafy material. Frequent severe cutting can damage it and reduce the food harvest.
items.draft: Dzhiani tsheo ya uri mumela muṅwe na muṅwe u ḓisa dzipea kana matari nga zwinzhi. U gwa zwinzhi nga tshifhinga tshinzhi zwi nga u tshinyadza na u fhungudza u vuna ha zwiḽiwa.
items.blindBackTranslation: Make a decision on whether each plant brings peas or leaves in large amounts. Cutting a lot at many times can damage it and reduce the yield of food.

items.sourceEnglish: Cowpea covers sunny gaps. Pigeon pea provides food and leafy material. Managed Sesbania sesban can supply taller temporary support.
items.draft: Cowpea i funekedza vhupo ha ḓuvha vhu si na mimela. Pigeon pea i ḓisa zwiḽiwa na matari. Sesbania sesban i ṱhogomelwaho i nga ṋea support plant ya tshifhinga tshipfufhi i lapfaho u fhirisa.
items.blindBackTranslation: Cowpea provides the ground in the sun [?] with no plants [?]. Pigeon pea brings food and leaves. A Sesbania sesban that is looked after can give a temporary support plant that lasts longer than the others [?].

items.sourceEnglish: Add suitable flowering and mulch plants. Keep the mango trunk clear and manage light, water and access.
items.draft: Engedzani mimela yo teaho ya maluvha na ya mulch. Ṱhogomelani uri mutshe wa muri wa mango u dzule u si na tshithu tshi u kwamaho, ni ṱhogomele tshedza, madi na vhupo ha u swika.
items.blindBackTranslation: Add suitable flowering plants and mulch. Make sure the trunk of the mango tree always has nothing touching it, and look after light, water and access space.

items.sourceEnglish: Count woody supports across the spaces between fruit trees. Sow suitable ground cover by area.
items.draft: Balani support plants dza muri nga vhupo vhu re vhukati ha miri ya mitshelo. Sembani ground cover yo teaho u tevhedza vhukhulu ha vhupo.
items.blindBackTranslation: Count the support plants of the tree by the space that is between the fruit trees. Plant ground cover that is suitable [?] following the size of the space.

items.sourceEnglish: There is no universal number per fruit tree. Adjust density to water, soil, plant size and your ability to prune and thin.
items.draft: A hu na nomboro i fanaho fhethu hoṱhe nga muri muthihi wa mitshelo. Lugisani density nga madi, mavu, vhukhulu ha mimela na vhukoni hanu ha u gwa malavhi na u ita thinning.
items.blindBackTranslation: There is no number that is the same everywhere for one fruit tree. Adjust density by water, soil, size of plants and your ability to cut the leaves/weeds [?] and to do thinning.

items.sourceEnglish: Conceptual guild teaching illustration; confirm plant identity with reliable botanical guidance.
items.draft: Tshifanyiso tsha muhumbulo tsha ngudo ya guild; khwaṱhisedzani uri ndi mumela ufhio ni tshi shumisa botanical guidance i fulufhedzeaho.
items.blindBackTranslation: Infographic of the idea of the guild lesson; confirm which plant [?] you are using when you use reliable botanical guidance.

items.sourceEnglish: Nitrogen Fixers: Choose and Manage Support Plants
items.draft: Nitrogen Fixers: Khethani ni Ṱhogomele Support Plants
items.blindBackTranslation: Nitrogen Fixers: Choose and Take Care of Support Plants

items.sourceEnglish: Legumes work with rhizobia in root nodules; fixation depends on suitable conditions.
items.draft: Legumes dzi shumisana na rhizobia kha nodules dza midzi; nitrogen fixation i ḓitika nga zwiimiswa zwo teaho.
items.blindBackTranslation: Legumes work together with rhizobia in root nodules; nitrogen fixation depends on suitable conditions.

items.sourceEnglish: Return useful cut material to the soil; nutrient release takes time.
items.draft: Vhuyedzani mavuni zwo gwiwaho zwi thusaho; u ṋewa ha nutrients hu dzhia tshifhinga.
items.blindBackTranslation: Return [?] to the soil what has rotted/matured that helps; the giving of nutrients takes time.

items.sourceEnglish: Use suitable seasonal cover, support shrubs and temporary trees.
items.draft: Shumisani cover yo teaho ya tshifhinga, support shrubs na miri ya tshifhinga tshipfufhi.
items.blindBackTranslation: Use suitable seasonal cover, support shrubs and short-lived trees.

items.sourceEnglish: Manage support density as plants grow; there is no universal count per fruit tree.
items.draft: Ṱhogomelani support density musi mimela i tshi gula; a hu na nomboro i fanaho fhethu hoṱhe nga muri muthihi wa mitshelo.
items.blindBackTranslation: Watch support density when the plants grow [?]; there is no number that is the same everywhere for one fruit tree.

items.sourceEnglish: When does nitrogen in cut legume material become available to other plants?
items.draft: Nitrogen kha zwo gwiwaho zwa legume i vha ya u wanala lini kha dziṅwe mimela?
items.blindBackTranslation: When does the nitrogen in cut legume material become available to other plants?

items.sourceEnglish: Immediately when it is cut
items.draft: Zwenezwo musi zwi tshi gwiwa
items.blindBackTranslation: Then when it is rotted/matured

items.sourceEnglish: As soil organisms decompose the material
items.draft: Musi zwipuka zwa mavuni zwi tshi ita decomposition ya zwo gwiwaho
items.blindBackTranslation: When the plant leaves do decomposition of what was cut

items.sourceEnglish: Only when the fruit tree touches the legume
items.draft: Fhedzi musi muri wa mitshelo u tshi kwama legume
items.blindBackTranslation: Only when the fruit tree touches the legume

items.sourceEnglish: It can never become available
items.draft: I nga si vhuye ya wanala
items.blindBackTranslation: It can never become available

items.sourceEnglish: Decomposition releases nutrients over time. The rate depends on the material and growing conditions.
items.draft: Decomposition i ṋea nutrients nga u dzhia tshifhinga. U ṱavhanya hayo hu ḓitika nga zwo gwiwaho na zwiimiswa zwa u gula.
items.blindBackTranslation: Decomposition gives nutrients by taking time. Its speed depends on what was cut and the growth conditions.

items.sourceEnglish: What should decide how many support plants you establish?
items.draft: Ndi mini zwine zwa fanela u ita tsheo ya uri ni simee support plants dzingafhani?
items.blindBackTranslation: What should you decide on, in order to decide which support plants to plant?

items.sourceEnglish: The same fixed number at every site
items.draft: Nomboro i fanaho i sa shanduki kha vhupo hunwe na hunwe
items.blindBackTranslation: The same number that does not change in every space

items.sourceEnglish: Water, soil, plant size and the care you can provide
items.draft: Madi, mavu, vhukhulu ha mimela na ṱhogomelo ine ni nga i ṋea
items.blindBackTranslation: Water, soil, size of the plants and the care that you can give

items.sourceEnglish: Always placing every support uphill
items.draft: U vhea tshifhinga tshoṱhe support plant yoṱhe nga tshipiḓa tsha thavha tshi re nṱha
items.blindBackTranslation: Always placing every support plant on the part of the hill that is above

items.sourceEnglish: Planting as many trees as will physically fit
items.draft: U sima miri yo vhalaho sa hune ya swika vhupo
items.blindBackTranslation: Planting as many trees as the place can hold

items.sourceEnglish: Support plants need resources and management too. Observe growth and competition, then adjust.
items.draft: Support plants na dzone dzi ṱoḓa zwishumiswa na ṱhogomelo. Sedzani u gula na u lwisana, ni dovhe ni lugise.
items.blindBackTranslation: Support plants also need resources and care. Check growth and competition, and then adjust.

items.sourceEnglish: The clip shows a branch cut: the support tree remains standing. Leave enough healthy foliage for the plant to recover.
items.draft: Vidio i sumbedza ḽavhi ḽo gwiwaho: support tree i dzula yo ima. Siani matari a re na mutakalo a swikelelaho uri mumela u kone u vhuya wa mela.
items.blindBackTranslation: The video shows a cut branch: the support tree stays standing. Leave healthy leaves that are enough so that the plant can come back and grow again.

items.sourceEnglish: Match cutting to the species. Avoid frequent severe cuts on pigeon pea, especially when growing it for peas.
items.draft: Gwani zwi tshi tevhedza lushaka lwa mumela. Dzivhani u gwa zwinzhi nga tshifhinga tshinzhi kha pigeon pea, nga maanḓa musi ni tshi i mela u itela dzipea.
items.blindBackTranslation: Cut according to the type of plant. Avoid cutting a lot at many times on pigeon pea, especially when you plant it for peas.

items.sourceEnglish: Mulch protects the surface, helps conserve moisture and returns organic material.
items.draft: Mulch i tsireledza nṱha ha mavu, i thusa u dzula ha madi mavuni nahone i vhuyedza zwithu zwi bvaho kha mimela.
items.blindBackTranslation: Mulch protects the top of the soil, helps water stay in the soil and returns things that come from plants.

items.sourceEnglish: Leave access for watering and inspection. Cut material into manageable pieces and keep observing moisture and decomposition.
items.draft: Siani vhupo ha u swika u itela u nwisa na u sedza. Gwani zwo gwiwaho zwi vhe zwipiḓa zwi lugaho, ni dzule ni tshi sedza madi a re mavuni na decomposition.
items.blindBackTranslation: Leave an access place for watering and looking. Cut the cut material into suitable pieces, and always watch the water that is in the soil and decomposition.

items.sourceEnglish: Obtain the correct cultivar. Bocking 14 does not spread by viable seed, but root pieces can regrow.
items.draft: Wanani cultivar ye ya lugaho. Bocking 14 a i andi nga viable seed, fhedzi zwipiḓa zwa midzi zwi nga mela hafhu.
items.blindBackTranslation: Find a cultivar that is suitable. Bocking 14 does not spread by viable seed, but pieces of roots can grow again.

items.sourceEnglish: Place it where it has room and sufficient moisture. Cut leaves as it recovers; do not crowd the young fruit tree.
items.draft: I siseni hune ya vha na vhupo na madi o swikelelaho. Gwani matari musi i tshi vhuya ya mela; ni songo ḓadza vhupo ha muri wa mitshelo une wa kha ḓi vha muṱuku.
items.blindBackTranslation: Put it where there is space and enough water. Cut the leaves when it comes to grow again; do not fill the space of the fruit tree that is still small.

items.sourceEnglish: Many ladybirds eat aphids; some parasitoid wasps attack crop pests. Flowering members such as African basil can add resources.
items.draft: Ladybirds nnzhi dzi ḽa aphids; dziṅwe parasitoid wasps dzi lwa na zwipuka zwi tshinyadzaho (pests) zwa zwijalo. Mimela ine ya vha na maluvha, sa African basil, i nga engedza zwishumiswa.
items.blindBackTranslation: Many ladybirds eat aphids; other parasitoid wasps fight insects that damage crops. Plants that have flowers, such as African basil, can add resources.

items.sourceEnglish: Watch which insects visit and whether damage changes. A flowering plant does not guarantee pest control.
items.draft: Sedzani zwipuka (insects) zwine zwa ḓa na uri tshinyalelo i a shanduka. Mumela une wa vha na maluvha a si khwaṱhisedzo ya u langa zwipuka zwi tshinyadzaho (pests).
items.blindBackTranslation: Watch the plants that come and whether the damage changes. A plant that has flowers is not a guarantee of controlling plants that damage [?].

items.sourceEnglish: Tulbaghia violacea has narrow leaves and lilac flowers. Place a clump where it has light and room to grow.
items.draft: Tulbaghia violacea i na matari a si a phara na maluvha a lilac. Vheani tshigwada hune ya wana tshedza na vhupo ha u gula.
items.blindBackTranslation: Tulbaghia violacea has leaves that are not broad [?] and lilac flowers. Plant a group where it gets light and space to grow.

items.sourceEnglish: Observe visiting insects. Do not promise that a ring of wild garlic will repel pests or cure an outbreak.
items.draft: Sedzani zwipuka (insects) zwi ḓaho. Ni songo vhuedza uri tshiringi tsha wild garlic tshi ḓo pandela zwipuka zwi tshinyadzaho (pests) kana u fhodza u ḓa ha zwipuka zwo vhalaho.
items.blindBackTranslation: Watch the plants/pests [?] that come. Do not promise that a row of wild garlic will chase away plants that damage or prevent the coming of many plants [?].

items.sourceEnglish: Conceptual guild teaching illustration; confirm plant identity with reliable botanical guidance.
items.draft: Tshifanyiso tsha muhumbulo tsha ngudo ya guild; khwaṱhisedzani uri ndi mumela ufhio ni tshi shumisa botanical guidance i fulufhedzeaho.
items.blindBackTranslation: Infographic of the idea of the guild lesson; confirm which plant [?] you are using when you use reliable botanical guidance.

items.sourceEnglish: Mulch Plants and Helpful Insects
items.draft: Mimela ya Mulch na Zwipuka zwi Thusaho
items.blindBackTranslation: Mulch Plants and Helpful Insects

items.sourceEnglish: Pruning cuts branches while keeping the support plant.
items.draft: U gwa malavhi hu gwa malavhi fhedzi, ngeno support plant i tshi dzula yo ima.
items.blindBackTranslation: Cutting leaves only cuts leaves, while the support plant stays standing.

items.sourceEnglish: Return suitable cut leaves as mulch while keeping the trunk clear.
items.draft: Vhuyedzani matari o gwiwaho a teaho sa mulch, ni tshi dzulisa mutshe wa muri u si na tshithu tshi u kwamaho.
items.blindBackTranslation: Return suitable cut leaves as mulch, while keeping the tree trunk with nothing touching it.

items.sourceEnglish: Bocking 14 does not spread by viable seed, but root pieces can regrow.
items.draft: Bocking 14 a i andi nga viable seed, fhedzi zwipiḓa zwa midzi zwi nga mela hafhu.
items.blindBackTranslation: Bocking 14 does not spread by viable seed, but pieces of roots can grow again.

items.sourceEnglish: Flowering plants can support useful insects; watch actual visits and crop damage.
items.draft: Mimela ya maluvha i nga thusa zwipuka zwi thusaho; sedzani u ḓa ha vhukuma na tshinyalelo ya zwijalo.
items.blindBackTranslation: Flower plants can help helpful insects; watch the real coming and the damage to crops.

items.sourceEnglish: What does the branch-cutting clip show?
items.draft: Vidio ya u gwa ḽavhi i sumbedza mini?
items.blindBackTranslation: What does the video of cutting a branch show?

items.sourceEnglish: Removing the whole support tree
items.draft: U bvisa support tree yoṱhe
items.blindBackTranslation: Removing the whole support tree

items.sourceEnglish: Pruning a retained support tree for light and mulch
items.draft: U gwa malavhi a support tree i sa bviswi, u itela tshedza na mulch
items.blindBackTranslation: Cutting the branches of a support tree that is not removed, for light and mulch

items.sourceEnglish: Harvesting the fruit tree
items.draft: U vuna muri wa mitshelo
items.blindBackTranslation: Harvesting the fruit tree

items.sourceEnglish: Proof that root competition has stopped
items.draft: Ndi vhuṱanzi ha uri u lwisana ha midzi ho fhela
items.blindBackTranslation: It is proof that competition of roots is finished

items.sourceEnglish: A branch falls, while the support tree remains standing. That is pruning and chop-and-drop.
items.draft: Ḽavhi ḽi a wela, ngeno support tree i dzula yo ima. Ndi u gwa malavhi na chop-and-drop.
items.blindBackTranslation: The branch falls, while the support tree stays standing. It is cutting branches and chop-and-drop.

items.sourceEnglish: How should you assess flowering plants used to support helpful insects?
items.draft: Ni fanela u ṱolisisa hani mimela ya maluvha i shumiswaho u thusa zwipuka (insects) zwi thusaho?
items.blindBackTranslation: How should you examine flowering plants that are used to help helpful plants/animals [?]?

items.sourceEnglish: Assume they will eliminate pests
items.draft: Dzhiani uri i ḓo fhelisa zwipuka zwi tshinyadzaho (pests)
items.blindBackTranslation: Assume that it will finish off the plants that damage [?]

items.sourceEnglish: Observe insect visitors and changes in crop damage
items.draft: Sedzani zwipuka zwi ḓaho na u shanduka ha tshinyalelo ya zwijalo
items.blindBackTranslation: Watch the insects that come and the change in crop damage

items.sourceEnglish: Remove all flowers before they open
items.draft: Bvisani maluvha oṱhe phanḓa ha u vula
items.blindBackTranslation: Remove all flowers before opening

items.sourceEnglish: Count every flowering plant as a nitrogen fixer
items.draft: Balani mumela muṅwe na muṅwe wa maluvha sa nitrogen fixer
items.blindBackTranslation: Count every flower plant as a nitrogen fixer

items.sourceEnglish: Flowers can supply resources, but their presence does not guarantee pest control.
items.draft: Maluvha a nga ṋea zwishumiswa, fhedzi u vha hayo a si khwaṱhisedzo ya u langa zwipuka zwi tshinyadzaho (pests).
items.blindBackTranslation: Flowers can give resources, but having them is not a guarantee of controlling plants that damage [?].

items.sourceEnglish: Combine the support functions your site needs: nitrogen fixation, food, mulch, flowers and ground cover. Some plants serve several functions.
items.draft: Ṱanganyani support functions ine vhupo hanu ha zwi ṱoḓa: nitrogen fixation, zwiḽiwa, mulch, maluvha na ground cover. Dziṅwe mimela i shuma mishumo minzhi.
items.blindBackTranslation: Combine support functions that your place needs: nitrogen fixation, food, mulch, flowers and ground cover. Some plants do many jobs.

items.sourceEnglish: Keep the trunk area and path open. Reassess each member as the mango and its neighbours grow.
items.draft: Siani vhupo ha mutshe wa muri na ndila vhu si na tshithu. Sedzani hafhu mumela muṅwe na muṅwe wa guild musi mango na mimela i re tsini nayo i tshi gula.
items.blindBackTranslation: Leave the space of the tree trunk and the path with nothing in it. Check again each plant of the guild when the mango and the plants near it are growing.

items.sourceEnglish: Keep its vines away from the young fruit tree and retain a route for care. Its roots also use water and nutrients.
items.draft: Dzulisani zwitwi zwayo kule na muri wa mitshelo une wa kha ḓi vha muṱuku ni siye ndila ya ṱhogomelo. Midzi yayo i shumisa na madi na nutrients.
items.blindBackTranslation: Keep its stems far from the fruit tree that is still small and leave a path of care. Its roots also use water and nutrients.

items.sourceEnglish: Where resources are tight, compare living cover with an ordinary mulch basin.
items.draft: Hune zwishumiswa zwi si zwinzhi, vhambedzani cover i tshilaho na mulch basin i ḓoweleaho.
items.blindBackTranslation: Where resources are not many, compare living cover with a mulch basin that is used to [?].

items.sourceEnglish: Plant into a suitable season, mulch and maintain establishment water. Keep the access gap open.
items.draft: Simani tshifhinga tsho teaho, ni vhee mulch ni tshi ṱhogomela madi a u thoma u mela nga murahu ha u sima. Siani vhupo ha u swika vhu si na tshithu.
items.blindBackTranslation: Plant at a suitable time, and put mulch while taking care of the water for starting to grow after planting. Leave the access place empty.

items.sourceEnglish: Start with the number of support plants you can care for. Observe survival and growth before adding more.
items.draft: Thomani nga nomboro ya support plants ine ni nga i ṱhogomela. Sedzani u tshila na u gula phanḓa ha u engedza dziṅwe.
items.blindBackTranslation: Start with the number of support plants that you can look after. Watch survival and growth before adding others.

items.sourceEnglish: Cut down selected competing supports to open space. Suitable cut material can stay as mulch: this is thinning through chop-and-drop.
items.draft: Gwani fhasi support plants dzo khethwaho dzi lwisanaho u itela u vula vhupo. Zwo gwiwaho zwo teaho zwi nga sala sa mulch: hezwi ndi u bvisa mimela (thinning) nga chop-and-drop.
items.blindBackTranslation: Cut down selected support plants that compete, to open space. Suitable cut material can remain as mulch: this is removing plants (thinning) by chop-and-drop.

items.sourceEnglish: Manage regrowth to keep the opening. Check light, soil moisture and growth; thinning does not instantly stop root competition.
items.draft: Ṱhogomelani u mela hafhu uri vhupo ho vuliwaho vhu dzule. Sedzani tshedza, madi a re mavuni na u gula; thinning a i imisi u lwisana ha midzi nga u ṱavhanya.
items.blindBackTranslation: Take care of regrowth so that the opened place stays. Watch light, water that is in the soil and growth; thinning does not quickly stop competition of roots.

items.sourceEnglish: Carry useful prunings back to established trees. Keep nearby plants only where they still perform well.
items.draft: Isani malavhi o gwiwaho a thusaho kha miri yo dzulaho kale. Dzulisani mimela i re tsini fhedzi hune i tshi kha di shuma zwavhuḓi.
items.blindBackTranslation: Carry cut leaves that help to trees that have stood for a long time. Keep the plants that are near only where they are still working well.

items.sourceEnglish: Mature fruit trees still need nutrients. Monitor growth, harvest and soil conditions; support plants do not remove that need.
items.draft: Miri ya mitshelo yo hulaho i kha ṱoḓa nutrients. Sedzani u gula, u vuna na zwiimiswa zwa mavu; support plants a dzi bvisi iyo ṱhoḓea.
items.blindBackTranslation: Grown fruit trees are still needing nutrients. Check growth, yield and soil conditions; support plants do not remove that need.

items.sourceEnglish: Check fruit-tree growth, shade, soil moisture, useful harvests and pest damage. Note what was cut, returned or removed.
items.draft: Sedzani u gula ha muri wa mitshelo, ṱhundu, madi a re mavuni, u vuna hu thusaho na tshinyalelo ya zwipuka zwi tshinyadzaho (pests). Nwalani zwo gwiwaho, zwo vhuyedzwaho kana zwo bviswaho.
items.blindBackTranslation: Check the growth of the fruit tree, pests [?], water that is in the soil, helpful yield and damage of plants that damage [?]. Write down what was cut, what was returned or what was removed.

items.sourceEnglish: Use these observations to change the layout and care. A plant earns its place through what it does here.
items.draft: Shumisani zwo sedzwaho izwi u shandukisa u ṱanganyiwa na ṱhogomelo. Mumela u wana vhupo hawo nga zwine wa zwi ita henefha.
items.blindBackTranslation: Use these things watched to change the combination and care. A plant finds its place by what it does there.

items.sourceEnglish: Conceptual guild teaching illustration; confirm plant identity with reliable botanical guidance.
items.draft: Tshifanyiso tsha muhumbulo tsha ngudo ya guild; khwaṱhisedzani uri ndi mumela ufhio ni tshi shumisa botanical guidance i fulufhedzeaho.

items.sourceEnglish: Build a Guild and Adjust It as It Grows

items.sourceEnglish: Watch the branch fall onto the cut leaves.
items.draft: Sedzani davhi ḽa muri ḽi tshi wela kha mauṋa o ṱemiwaho.
items.blindBackTranslation: Look at a branch of a tree falling onto the cut leaves.

items.sourceEnglish: Chop-and-Drop for Light and Mulch
items.draft: Chop-and-Drop ya Tshedza na Mulch
items.blindBackTranslation: Chop-and-Drop of Shade and Mulch

items.sourceEnglish: Prune a support tree and return suitable leafy cuttings to the soil. The clip shows a branch cut: the support tree remains standing. Leave enough healthy foliage for the plant to recover.  Match cutting to the species. Avoid frequent severe cuts on pigeon pea, especially when growing it for peas. Which plant needs a cut—and how much?
items.draft: Temani madavhi a support tree ni vhuyedze mavuni zwipiḓa zwa mauṋa zwo teaho. Vhidio i sumbedza davhi ḽo ṱemiwaho: support tree i dzula i tshi eme. Sia mauṋa a mutakalo a ringaneaho uri tshimela tshi kone u vha na maanda hafhu. Ṱemani u ya nga species. Ni songo ṱema pigeon pea nga maanda na lunzhi, zwihulwane musi ni tshi i melela u wana peas. Ndi tshimela tshifhio tshine tsha ṱoḓa u ṱemiwa, nahone ndi zwingafhani?
items.blindBackTranslation: Cut the branches of the support tree and return to the soil suitable pieces of leaves. The video shows a cut branch: the support tree remains standing. Leave healthy leaves that are sufficient so that the plant can be strong again. Cut according to species. Do not cut pigeon pea strongly and often, especially when you are growing it to get peas. Which plant is the one that needs to be cut, and how much is it?

items.sourceEnglish: Keep Mulch Off the Trunk
items.draft: Dzulisani Mulch Kule na Tsinde ḽa Muri
items.blindBackTranslation: Keep Mulch Away from the Trunk of the Tree

items.sourceEnglish: Spread suitable cut material over the soil, with the trunk and root collar clear.
items.draft: Andani zwiṱemiwa zwo teaho nṱha ha mavu, tsinde ḽa muri na root collar zwi tshi dzula zwi sa fukiwi.
items.blindBackTranslation: Spread suitable cut pieces above the soil, with the trunk of the tree and the root collar always remaining uncovered.

items.sourceEnglish: Keep Mulch Off the Trunk
items.draft: Dzulisani Mulch Kule na Tsinde ḽa Muri
items.blindBackTranslation: Keep Mulch Away from the Trunk of the Tree

items.sourceEnglish: Mulch protects the surface, helps conserve moisture and returns organic material.  Leave access for watering and inspection. Cut material into manageable pieces and keep observing moisture and decomposition. Is the root collar still clear?
items.draft: Mulch i tsireledza nṱha ha mavu, i thusa u vhulunga madi a re mavuni nahone i vhuyedza organic material. Sia ndila ya u dzhena ya u unela madi na u sedzulusa. Ṱemani zwiṱemiwa zwi vhe zwipiḓa zwine na kona u zwi langa, ni dzule ni tshi sedzulusa madi a re mavuni na decomposition. Naa root collar i kha ḓi dzula i sa fukiwi?
items.blindBackTranslation: Mulch protects the top of the soil, it helps to keep the water that is in the soil, and it also returns organic material. Leave a way in for taking in water and for checking. Cut the cuttings/plants into pieces that you are able to manage, and keep checking the water that is in the soil and the decomposition. Is the root collar still always uncovered? [Literal: 'i kha ḓi dzula i sa fukiwi' = 'it still keeps staying not covered']

items.sourceEnglish: Choose the Right Comfrey
items.draft: Khethani Comfrey i Teaho
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose Suitable Comfrey

items.sourceEnglish: Bocking 14 comfrey can supply cut leaves for mulch.
items.draft: Bocking 14 comfrey i nga ṋea mauṋa o ṱemiwaho a u shumisa sa mulch.
items.blindBackTranslation: Bocking 14 comfrey can give cut leaves to use as mulch.

items.sourceEnglish: Choose the Right Comfrey
items.draft: Khethani Comfrey i Teaho
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose Suitable Comfrey

items.sourceEnglish: Obtain the correct cultivar. Bocking 14 does not spread by viable seed, but root pieces can regrow.  Place it where it has room and sufficient moisture. Cut leaves as it recovers; do not crowd the young fruit tree. Is this a good permanent place for the clump?
items.draft: Wanani cultivar yo teaho. Bocking 14 a i andi nga viable seed, fhedzi zwipiḓa zwa midzi zwi nga mela hafhu. I vheeni fhethu hune ha vha na fhethu ha u hula na madi o linganaho. Ṱemani mauṋa musi i tshi vhuyelela; ni songo ita uri i hwele muri wa mitshelo une wa kha ḓi vha muṱuku. Naa heyi ndi fhethu ha tshifhinga tshoṱhe ho teaho ha tshigwada itshi?
items.blindBackTranslation: Find a suitable cultivar. Bocking 14 does not give viable seed, but pieces of roots can grow again. Put it where there is a place to grow and sufficient water. Cut the leaves when it returns/regrows; do not let it cover the fruit tree that is still small. Is this a suitable all-time/permanent place [?] for this group?

items.sourceEnglish: Observe Helpful Insects
items.draft: Sedzulusani Zwipuka (insects) zwi Thusaho
items.blindBackTranslation: Check Helpful Insects

items.sourceEnglish: Flowers can provide resources for useful insects.
items.draft: Maluvha a nga ṋea zwithu zwine zwipuka zwi thusaho (insects) zwa vha zwi tshi zwi ṱoḓa.
items.blindBackTranslation: Flowers can give things that helpful insects need [?: 'zwipuka' read as insects].

items.sourceEnglish: Observe Helpful Insects
items.draft: Sedzulusani Zwipuka (insects) zwi Thusaho
items.blindBackTranslation: Check Helpful Insects

items.sourceEnglish: Many ladybirds eat aphids; some parasitoid wasps attack crop pests. Flowering members such as African basil can add resources.  Watch which insects visit and whether damage changes. A flowering plant does not guarantee pest control. What is the insect actually doing?
items.draft: Ladybirds dzinzhi dzi ḽa aphids; dziṅwe parasitoid wasps dzi lwa na zwikhakhisi (pests) zwa zwimela zwa u lima. Miraḓo ya guild i re na maluvha, sa African basil, i nga engedza zwithu zwi thusaho. Sedzani zwipuka (insects) zwine zwa dzhena na arali u tshinyea hu tshi shanduka. Tshimela tshi re na maluvha, a tshi khwathisedzi u lawula zwikhakhisi. Naa tshipuka itshi tshi khou ita mini ngoho?
items.blindBackTranslation: Ladybirds are many [?: dzinzhi = many/most; possibly 'Ladybirds eat many'] of the aphids; other parasitoid wasps fight with the pests of cultivated plants. Members of the guild that have flowers, like African basil, can increase things that help. Look at the animals/creatures [?] that come in and if damage is changing. A plant that has flowers does not guarantee control of pests. So what is this creature/plant [?] actually doing?

items.sourceEnglish: Give Flowers Their Space
items.draft: Ṋeani Maluvha Fhethu havho
items.blindBackTranslation: Give Flowers Their Place

items.sourceEnglish: Wild garlic can be a flowering member where the site suits it.
items.draft: Wild garlic i nga vha muraḓo u bvisaho maluvha hune fhethu ha tendelana nayo.
items.blindBackTranslation: Wild garlic can be a flower-producing member where the place agrees with it.

items.sourceEnglish: Give Flowers Their Space
items.draft: Ṋeani Maluvha Fhethu havho
items.blindBackTranslation: Give Flowers Their Place

items.sourceEnglish: Tulbaghia violacea has narrow leaves and lilac flowers. Place a clump where it has light and room to grow.  Observe visiting insects. Do not promise that a ring of wild garlic will repel pests or cure an outbreak. Where can flowers grow without crowding?
items.draft: Tulbaghia violacea i na mauṋa a re ṱhukhu na maluvha a rangi ya lilac. Vheani tshigwada tsha zwimela fhethu hune ha vha na tshedza na fhethu ha u hula. Sedzulusani zwipuka (insects) zwi dzhenaho. Ni songo fulufhedzisa uri tshiviringi tsha wild garlic tshi ḓo thivhela zwikhakhisi (pests) kana u fhodza u engedzea ha zwikhakhisi hu ṱavhanyaho. Ndi ngafhi hune maluvha a nga mela hu si na u hwelana?
items.blindBackTranslation: Tulbaghia violacea has small/short leaves and flowers of lilac colour. Put a group of plants where there is light and a place to grow. Review the plants that come in. Do not promise that a ring of wild garlic will prevent pests or stop the quick increase of pests. Where can the flowers grow without getting in each other's way/tangling [?]?

items.sourceEnglish: Bring the Jobs Together
items.draft: Tanganyani Mishumo Fhethu Huthihi
items.blindBackTranslation: Combine Functions in One Place

items.sourceEnglish: Choose useful partners while protecting the mango's growing space.
items.draft: Khethani zwimela zwi thusaho zwine zwa shumisana nayo musi ni tshi tsireledza fhethu ha u hula ha mango.
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose helping plants that work together with it when you protect the growing place of mangoes.

items.sourceEnglish: Bring the Jobs Together
items.draft: Tanganyani Mishumo Fhethu Huthihi
items.blindBackTranslation: Combine Functions in One Place

items.sourceEnglish: Combine the support functions your site needs: nitrogen fixation, food, mulch, flowers and ground cover. Some plants serve several functions.  Keep the trunk area and path open. Reassess each member as the mango and its neighbours grow. Does each member have space and a job?
items.draft: Tanganyani support functions dzine fhethu hanu ha dzi ṱoḓa: nitrogen fixation, zwiḓiwa, mulch, maluvha na zwimela zwi fukaho mavu. Zwiṅwe zwimela zwi shuma mishumo minzhi. Dzulisani fhethu ha tsinde na ndila zwo vuleaho. Sedzulusani muraḓo muṅwe na muṅwe musi mango na zwimela zwi re tsini nayo zwi tshi hula. Naa muraḓo muṅwe na muṅwe u na fhethu na mushumo?
items.blindBackTranslation: Combine support functions that your place needs: nitrogen fixation, food, mulch, flowers and plants that cover the soil. Some plants do many functions. Keep the place of the trunk and the path open. Check each member when the mango and the plants that are near it are growing. Does each member have a place and a function?

items.sourceEnglish: Food Cover Also Competes
items.draft: Zwiḓiwa zwi Fukaho Zwi Dovha Zwa Pikisana
items.blindBackTranslation: Soil-Covering Foods Also Compete

items.sourceEnglish: Sweet potato can cover ground and provide food in a suitable sunny space.
items.draft: Sweet potato i nga fuka mavu nahone ya ṋea zwiḓiwa fhethu ho teaho hune ḓuvha ḽa swika.
items.blindBackTranslation: Sweet potato can cover the soil and give food in a suitable place where the sun arrives.

items.sourceEnglish: Food Cover Also Competes
items.draft: Zwiḓiwa zwi Fukaho Zwi Dovha Zwa Pikisana
items.blindBackTranslation: Soil-Covering Foods Also Compete

items.sourceEnglish: Keep its vines away from the young fruit tree and retain a route for care. Its roots also use water and nutrients.  Where resources are tight, compare living cover with an ordinary mulch basin. Is this cover helping the tree establish?
items.draft: Dzulisani mitsinde yayo i kule na muri wa mitshelo une wa kha ḓi vha muṱuku, ni sie ndila ya u u londa. Midzi yayo i dovha ya shumisa madi na nutrients. Hune zwiko zwi si zwinzhi, vhambedzani zwimela zwi tshilaho zwi fukaho mavu na mulch basin ya ḓoweleo. Naa zwimela izwi zwi fukaho zwi khou thusa muri u dzhia midzi na u dzula zwavhuḓi?
items.blindBackTranslation: Plant its stems far from the fruit tree that is still small, and leave a way to care for it. Its roots also use water and nutrients. Where resources are not many, compare living plants that cover the soil with a mulch basin that is used to [?: 'ya ḓoweleo' unclear, perhaps 'of the usual/customary kind']. Are these covering plants helping the tree to take roots and to stay well?

items.sourceEnglish: First, Establish the Guild
items.draft: Thoma nga u Imisa Guild
items.blindBackTranslation: Start by Establishing the Guild

items.sourceEnglish: Start while the young fruit tree and its support plants have enough light and water.
items.draft: Thomani guild musi muri wa mitshelo une wa kha ḓi vha muṱuku na support plants dzawo zwi tshi na tshedza na madi zwo linganaho.
items.blindBackTranslation: Take (or: Harvest) the guild when the fruit tree that is still small and its support plants have sufficient light and water. [?: 'Thomani' is ambiguous; could be 'Choose/Start/Pick' the guild]

items.sourceEnglish: First, Establish the Guild
items.draft: Thoma nga u Imisa Guild
items.blindBackTranslation: Start by Establishing the Guild

items.sourceEnglish: Plant into a suitable season, mulch and maintain establishment water. Keep the access gap open.  Start with the number of support plants you can care for. Observe survival and growth before adding more. Can you care for every plant through establishment?
items.draft: Dzimani kha tshifhinga tsho teaho, ni fukele nga mulch ni dzule ni tshi unela madi a tshifhinga tsha u dzhia midzi. Dzulisani fhethu ha u dzhena ho vuleaho. Thomani nga tshivhalo tsha support plants dzine na dzi londa. Sedzulusani u tshila na u hula ni sa athu u engedza dziṅwe. Naa ni nga londa tshimela tshiṅwe na tshiṅwe lwa tshifhinga tsha u dzhia midzi?
items.blindBackTranslation: Plant at a suitable time, cover with mulch, and always water during the time of taking root. Keep the entry place open. Start with the number of support plants that you can look after. Check survival and growth before you add others. Can you look after every plant for the whole period of taking root?

items.sourceEnglish: Thin as the Fruit Tree Grows
items.draft: Thinning Musi Muri wa Mitshelo u Tshi Hula
items.blindBackTranslation: Thinning When the Fruit Tree Is Growing

items.sourceEnglish: When pruning is no longer enough, reduce selected support plants. Cut down selected competing supports to open space. Suitable cut material can stay as mulch: this is thinning through chop-and-drop.  Manage regrowth to keep the opening. Check light, soil moisture and growth; thinning does not instantly stop root competition. Which support plants should now give way?
items.draft: Musi u ṱema madavhi zwi tshi sa tsha ringana, fhungudzani support plants dzo khethiwaho. Ṱemani support plants dzo khethiwaho dzi pikisanaho dzi wele fhasi, uri hu vule fhethu. Zwiṱemiwa zwo teaho zwi nga sia zwi tshi vha mulch: heyi ndi thinning nga chop-and-drop. Langani u mela hafhu uri fhethu ho vuleaho hu dzule. Sedzani tshedza, madi a re mavuni na u hula; thinning a i imisi nga u ṱavhanya u pikisana ha midzi. Ndi support plants dzifhio dzine dza fanela u bva zwino?
items.blindBackTranslation: When cutting branches is no longer enough, reduce the chosen support plants. Cut down the chosen support plants that are competing, so that they fall down, so that a place opens up. Suitable cut pieces can be left to become mulch: this is thinning by chop-and-drop. Manage regrowth so that the opened place stays. Watch light, water that is in the soil, and growth; thinning does not stop root competition quickly. Which support plants should be removed now?

items.sourceEnglish: Move Support Into the Light
items.draft: Fambisani Support Plants kha Tshedza
items.blindBackTranslation: Move Support Plants into Light

items.sourceEnglish: As shade increases, renew sun-loving support plants in open edges and younger plantings.
items.draft: Musi ndindi i tshi engedzea, vusuludzani support plants dzi funaho ḓuvha kha mathibo o vuleaho na kha zwidzimiwa zwiswa.
items.blindBackTranslation: When the shade increases, renew the sun-loving support plants in open edges and in new gaps [?: 'zwidzimiwa' read as gaps/places planted].

items.sourceEnglish: Move Support Into the Light
items.draft: Fambisani Support Plants kha Tshedza
items.blindBackTranslation: Move Support Plants into Light

items.sourceEnglish: Carry useful prunings back to established trees. Keep nearby plants only where they still perform well.  Mature fruit trees still need nutrients. Monitor growth, harvest and soil conditions; support plants do not remove that need. Where is the next useful sunny space?
items.draft: Ḓisani madavhi a thusaho o ṱemiwaho kha miri yo dzhiaho midzi. Dzulisani zwimela zwa tsini fhedzi hune zwi tshi kha ḓi shuma zwavhuḓi. Miri ya mitshelo yo hulaho i kha ḓi ṱoḓa nutrients. Sedzulusani u hula, mavuno na nyimele ya mavu; support plants a dzi fhelisi u ṱoḓa nutrients ha miri. Ndi ngafhi fhethu hu tevhelaho hune ha vha na ḓuvha, hune ha nga thusa?
items.blindBackTranslation: Bring helpful pits/holes [?] that have been cut/pruned to trees that have taken roots. Plant plants that are near only where they are still working well. Fruit trees that have grown still need nutrients. Review growing, harvests and the condition of the soil; support plants do not end the need for nutrients of the trees. Where is the next place where there is a day, that could help? [?: 'ḓuvha' = day/sun; possibly 'sunny spot']

items.sourceEnglish: Let Observation Decide
items.draft: Tendelani Zwine na Zwi Vhona Zwi Dzhie Phetho
items.blindBackTranslation: Allow What You See to Make the Decision

items.sourceEnglish: Keep a short record of how the guild performs.
items.draft: Dzulani ni tshi ṅwala zwipfufhi zwa uri guild i khou shuma hani.
items.blindBackTranslation: Always write short notes on how the guild is working.

items.sourceEnglish: Let Observation Decide
items.draft: Tendelani Zwine na Zwi Vhona Zwi Dzhie Phetho
items.blindBackTranslation: Allow What You See to Make the Decision

items.sourceEnglish: Check fruit-tree growth, shade, soil moisture, useful harvests and pest damage. Note what was cut, returned or removed.  Use these observations to change the layout and care. A plant earns its place through what it does here. What evidence would make you change the guild?
items.draft: Sedzani u hula ha muri wa mitshelo, muvhundu, madi a re mavuni, mavuno a thusaho na u tshinyea nga zwikhakhisi (pests). Ṅwalani zwo ṱemiwaho, zwo vhuyedzwaho kana zwo bviswaho. Shumisani zwo sedzwaho izwi u shandukisa ndila ya u dzudzanya na u londa. Tshimela tshi wana fhethu hatsho nga zwine tsha zwi ita fhano. Ndi vhuṱanzi vhufhio vhune ha ni ita uri ni shandukise guild?
items.blindBackTranslation: Look at the growing of the fruit tree, the soil, the water that is in the soils, the helpful soils/harvests [?], and damage by pests. Write down what has been cut, what has been replaced/returned, or what has been removed. Use these things observed to change the way of arranging and caring for [it]. A plant finds its place by what it does here. What is the evidence that makes you change the guild?

items.sourceEnglish: Plan One Real Guild
items.draft: Dzudzanyani Guild Ithihi ya Ngoho
items.blindBackTranslation: Arrange One Real Guild

items.sourceEnglish: Choose one fruit tree and mark a layout you can manage.
items.draft: Khethani muri muthihi wa mitshelo ni maka ndila ya u dzudzanya ine na nga i langa.
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose one fruit tree and mark a way of arranging that you can manage.

items.sourceEnglish: Plan One Real Guild
items.draft: Dzudzanyani Guild Ithihi ya Ngoho
items.blindBackTranslation: Arrange One Real Guild

items.sourceEnglish: Record the tree, site conditions and missing jobs. Name the support species fully, mark the starting number and leave access.  Write down what will trigger pruning or thinning. Agree the species list with the project team where required. Can someone else explain your plan back to you?
items.draft: Ṅwalani muri, nyimele dza fhethu na mishumo yo shayeaho. Ṅwalani madzina a support species o fhelelaho, ni maka tshivhalo tsha u thoma ni sie fhethu ha u dzhena. Ṅwalani zwine zwa ḓo ita uri hu ṱemiwe madavhi kana hu ite thinning. Tendelanani nga mutevhe wa species na tshigwada tsha projeke hune zwa ṱoḓea. Naa muṅwe muthu a nga ni ṱalutshedza hafhu pulane yanu?
items.blindBackTranslation: Write the tree, the conditions of the place and the missing functions. Write the names of the complete support species, and mark the starting number and leave a place to enter. Write what will cause branches to be cut or thinning to be done. Agree on the list of species with the project group where it is needed. Can someone explain your plan to you again?

items.sourceEnglish: Plant, Observe, Adjust
items.draft: Dzimani, Sedzulusani, Shandukisani
items.blindBackTranslation: Plant, Check, Change

items.sourceEnglish: Start one suitable guild and care for it through its first stage.
items.draft: Thomani guild ithihi yo teaho ni i londe lwa tshifhinga tsha u thoma.
items.blindBackTranslation: Start one suitable guild and look after it for the starting period.

items.sourceEnglish: Plant, Observe, Adjust
items.draft: Dzimani, Sedzulusani, Shandukisani
items.blindBackTranslation: Plant, Check, Change

items.sourceEnglish: Use the right species, a manageable number of plants and room to grow. Return useful biomass and protect the fruit tree.  Review the planting as crowns expand. Keep, cut, replace or remove each support plant when its role changes. What will you do first—and when will you review it?
items.draft: Shumisani species dzo teaho, tshivhalo tsha zwimela tshine na tshi langa na fhethu ha u hula. Vhuyedzani biomass i thusaho ni tsireledze muri wa mitshelo. Sedzulusani zwo dzimiwaho musi crowns dzi tshi andela. Dzulisani, ṱemani, shandukisani kana bvisani support plant tshiṅwe na tshiṅwe musi mushumo wa tsho u tshi shanduka. Ndi mini hune na ḓo thoma nga hone, nahone ni ḓo sedzulusa lini?
items.blindBackTranslation: Use suitable species, the number of plants that you manage and a place to grow. Return helpful biomass and protect the fruit tree. Check what was planted when crowns are spreading. Keep, cut, change or remove each support plant when its function has changed. What will you start with, and when will you check?
